title: Heterobifunctional proteomimetic polymers for targeted protein degradation.
authors: Wang, Max M; Truica, Mihai I; Gattis, Brayley S; Oktawiec, Julia; Sagar, Vinay; Basu, Ananya A; Bertin, Paul A; Zhang, Xiaoyu; Abdulkadir, Sarki A; Gianneschi, Nathan C
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究靶向蛋白降解的聚合物平台，虽涉及转录因子MYC但无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The burgeoning field of targeted protein degradation (TPD) has opened new avenues for modulating the activity of previously undruggable proteins of interest. To date, TPD has been dominated by small molecules containing separate linked domains for protein engagement and recruitment of cellular degradation machinery. The process of identifying active compounds has required tedious optimization and has been successful largely against a limited set of targets with well-defined, suitable docking pockets. Here we present a polymer chemistry approach termed the HYbrid DegRAding Copolymer (HYDRAC) to overcome standing challenges associated with the development of TPD. These copolymers densely display either peptide-based or small molecule-derived degradation inducers and target-binding peptide sequences for the selective degradation of disease-associated proteins. HYDRACs are synthesized in a facile manner, are modular in design, and are highly selective. Using the intrinsically disordered transcription factor MYC as an initial proof-of-concept, difficult to drug protein target, HYDRACs containing a MYC-inhibitory peptide copolymerized with a validated degron, showed robust and selective degradation of the target protein. Treatment of tumor-bearing mice with MYC-targeted HYDRACs showed decreased cell proliferation and increased tumor apoptosis, leading to significantly suppressed tumor growth in vivo . The versatility of the platform was demonstrated by substituting the degron for recruiters of three different E3 ligases (VHL, KEAP1, and CRBN), which all maintained MYC degradation. To demonstrate generalizability, HYDRACs were further designed against a second elusive target of clinical interest, KRAS, by employing a consensus RAS binding motif. RAS-targeted HYDRACs showed degradation in two cell lines harboring separate KRAS alleles, suggesting potential pan-KRAS activity. We envision the HYDRAC platform as a generalizable approach to developing degraders of proteins of interest, greatly expanding the therapeutic armamentarium for TPD.
abstract_zh: 靶向蛋白降解（targeted protein degradation, TPD）这一新兴领域为调控此前难以成药的目标蛋白活性开辟了新途径。迄今为止，TPD主要依赖于包含独立连接域的小分子，用于蛋白结合和招募细胞降解机制。活性化合物的识别过程需要繁琐的优化，且主要针对具有明确、合适结合口袋的有限靶点取得成功。在此，我们提出一种聚合物化学方法，称为杂化降解共聚物（HYbrid DegRAding Copolymer, HYDRAC），以克服TPD开发中面临的长期挑战。这些共聚物密集展示基于肽或小分子衍生的降解诱导剂和靶标结合肽序列，用于选择性降解疾病相关蛋白。HYDRACs合成简便、设计模块化且高度选择性。以内在无序转录因子MYC作为初步概念验证的难成药蛋白靶点，含有MYC抑制肽与已验证降解子共聚的HYDRACs显示出对目标蛋白的稳健且选择性降解。用MYC靶向HYDRACs处理荷瘤小鼠，结果显示细胞增殖减少、肿瘤凋亡增加，从而在体内显著抑制肿瘤生长。该平台的通用性通过将降解子替换为三种不同E3连接酶（VHL、KEAP1和CRBN）的招募子得到验证，这些变体均维持了MYC降解活性。为证明普适性，HYDRACs进一步针对临床关注的另一个难以捉摸的靶点KRAS进行设计，采用共识RAS结合基序。RAS靶向HYDRACs在携带不同KRAS等位基因的两个细胞系中显示出降解效果，提示潜在的泛KRAS活性。我们设想HYDRAC平台作为一种通用方法，用于开发目标蛋白的降解剂，极大扩展TPD的治疗武器库。
